name: Huang Tengqi
profile: Listed on the Hurun China 2010 rich list (approx. US$150m) as founder of Xinlianxin Group (黄腾其), with interests in supermarkets, agricultural cultivation and property investment. No further public information could be verified in English or Chinese web searches.
notes: Very low public footprint; only appearance is Hurun China 2010. Company's Chinese name not confirmed (searches for 新联心 returned nothing relevant). Would need Chinese corporate registries (e.g. Qichacha) to verify; not a strong podcast lead.

name: Mayur Mukundlal Desai
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2018 (approx. US$144m) with wealth from Infibeam Avenues, the Ahmedabad fintech/e-commerce company behind the CCAvenue payment gateway. Infibeam's March 2019 shareholding filing lists 'Mayur Mukundlal Desai' as a public shareholder holding more than 1%. Not a director or executive of the company.
interesting_fact: Appears in Infibeam Avenues' official March 2019 shareholding pattern among public shareholders owning more than 1% of the company.
notes: Passive investor in Infibeam rather than founder (founders are Vishal Mehta and Vishwas Patel). No public profile found; identity beyond the shareholding filing unverified. Company was renamed AvenuesAI in 2025-26.

name: Rita Kishore Sinha
current_role: Non-Executive Director, SIS Limited (Security and Intelligence Services India)
profile: Rita Kishore Sinha is a long-time director and major shareholder (~16%) of SIS Ltd, the Patna-founded security, facility-management and cash-logistics group started by her husband, journalist-turned-politician RK Sinha. SIS is now one of India's largest private employers, with FY2026 revenue of about ₹15,982 crore; her son Rituraj Sinha is Group MD.
interesting_fact: SIS grew from a small Patna security agency into a multinational group; the company says revenue rose from ₹25 crore in 2002 to ₹15,982 crore in FY2026, with operations including Australia (MSS) and a cash-logistics JV with Prosegur.
deep_cut_fact: She is a lawyer by training: she holds a BA in Hindi and an LLB from Ranchi University, has around 32 years of legal experience and is enrolled with the Supreme Court Bar Association.
notes: Low personal media profile; the public face of SIS is son Rituraj Kishore Sinha (Group MD). Best route is SIS media relations.

name: Zhou Xiaodi
profile: Listed on the Hurun China rich list 2005-2007 (approx. US$130m) as head of Zhoushi Group (周小弟, 周氏集团), a real-estate developer. No further verifiable public information was found in English or Chinese searches.
notes: Very low footprint; last rich-list appearance 2007. Region and current status of the company unknown. Would need Chinese corporate registry research; not a strong podcast lead.

name: Rene R. Joyce
current_role: Director, Targa Resources Corp. (NYSE: TRGP); founding CEO (2005-2011)
profile: Rene Joyce is the founding CEO of Targa Resources, the Houston midstream natural-gas and NGL company he led from its 2005 formation until 2011, then served as executive chairman (2012-2014) and remains a director. Earlier he ran Tejas Gas pipeline subsidiaries and Shell's Coral Energy units, and has sat on the boards of Apache and Core Labs.
interesting_fact: Targa, which he built from a 2005 private-equity-backed startup, is now one of North America's largest independent midstream companies; in 2026 it signed 20-year integrated midstream agreements with ExxonMobil in the Permian Delaware Basin.
deep_cut_fact: He is both an engineer and a lawyer: BS in mechanical engineering from LSU (1970) and a JD from Loyola University New Orleans (1974); he sits on the LSU Foundation National Board and is a member of LSU's Society for Engineering Excellence.
notes: Highly relevant to energy theme (natural gas midstream, Permian). Low personal media profile; route via Targa corporate/investor relations or LSU engineering network. A Targa proxy noted a planned board retirement at an annual meeting—confirm current board status in latest proxy.

name: Rashmita Patnaik
current_role: Director/promoter, Falcon Marine Exports Ltd (Bhubaneswar, Odisha)
profile: Rashmita Patnaik is a long-serving director and promoter of Falcon Marine Exports, a Bhubaneswar-based seafood (mainly shrimp) processor and exporter founded in 1986 by Tara Ranjan and Prava Ranjan Patnaik. She also holds directorships in group companies such as Falcon Drinks, Falcon Real Estate and Falcon Holdings. Listed on Hurun India 2018-2019 (~US$120m).
interesting_fact: Falcon Marine Exports, set up in Odisha in 1986, grew into one of India's leading shrimp exporters and has been recognised in MPEDA's export awards (2018-19 awardee list).
notes: Non-executive, very private; company's public face is chairman Tara Ranjan Patnaik (Priyanka Mohanty named Joint MD in 2026). Board data from third-party MCA aggregators (qorpiq.com). No published company email found on falconmarine.in.

name: Ravinder Kumar Agarwal
current_role: Possibly Managing Director, Ravi Foods Pvt Ltd (Dukes India) — unconfirmed link to 'Singhania Foods International'
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2019 (~US$120m) in food & beverages under 'Singhania Foods International', a company name that could not be found online. The most prominent match is Ravinder Agarwal, MD of Ravi Foods Pvt Ltd (Dukes brand biscuits, wafers, confectionery), which says it runs 17 plants with ~5,000 staff; the identity link is unverified.
interesting_fact: If the Dukes match is right: Dukes says he has championed millet-based products and built RFPL to 17 manufacturing units under a 'Making in India, for the world' ethos.
notes: Identity ambiguous: several Ravinder/Ravindra Kumar Agarwals exist (e.g. one at Suryajyoti Spinning Mills). Contact listed is Dukes' general email and only relevant if he is the Dukes MD — verify before outreach.

name: Jean-Marie Mognetti
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, CoinShares PLC (Nasdaq: CSHR)
profile: French-born Jean-Marie Mognetti co-founded CoinShares, Europe's largest digital-asset manager, which launched the world's first regulated Bitcoin ETP in 2015 and holds ~34% EMEA crypto-ETP market share. A former quantitative commodity trader, he has led the Jersey-registered firm since 2014, including its 2024 acquisition of Valkyrie and its move to a US listing.
interesting_fact: CoinShares launched the world's first regulated Bitcoin exchange-traded product in 2015—roughly a decade before US spot Bitcoin ETFs were approved.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he was a quant commodity trader at Hermes Commodities Fund Managers, after a Master's in Mathematical Trading and Finance from Sir John Cass Business School; Blockworks reports oil-industry/JPMorgan veterans Danny Masters and Russell Newton brought him into what became CoinShares in 2012.
notes: Frequent conference speaker and media guest — good podcast fit (bitcoin mining/energy angle via CoinShares' mining research and ETPs). Background story: blockworks.co 'Gone Crypto: Mognetti and the Birth of CoinShares'.

name: Anand Parekh
current_role: Founder and CEO, Alyeska Investment Group (Chicago hedge fund)
profile: Anand Parekh founded Chicago-based multi-manager hedge fund Alyeska Investment Group in 2007 after serving as a partner at Citadel, where he built and ran the Global Equities and Reinsurance businesses; earlier he was an MD at Deutsche Bank. His SEC 10%-owner filings in FrontView REIT and Strawberry Fields REIT reflect Alyeska fund holdings, not operating roles.
interesting_fact: Reuters reported in 2007 that the ex-Citadel equities head was launching Alyeska with about $1.5 billion of backing from Deutsche Bank—an unusually large seed for a debut fund.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a quant-minded hedge fund founder, he holds a BS in both Mathematics and English Literature from the University of Michigan.

public_contacts.value: https://www.alyeskagroup.com/ (Alyeska Investment Group, 77 W Wacker Dr, Chicago — firm office)

notes: Very low-profile hedge fund manager; Alyeska's site is a bare address page. Has appeared as a speaker for Bessemer Trust. Not to be confused with Dr. Anand Parekh (health policy). Name in SEC filings: Anand Christopher Parekh.

name: Stefano Caroti
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Deckers Brands (NYSE: DECK)
profile: Stefano Caroti became CEO of Deckers Brands (HOKA, UGG, Teva) in August 2024, succeeding Dave Powers. He joined Deckers in 2015 as President of Omni-Channel, then served as Chief Commercial Officer and interim HOKA president during the brand's breakout growth. Before that he was CCO/MD at PUMA (2008-2014) and spent years in senior roles at Nike.
interesting_fact: He personally ran HOKA as interim president (2022-2024) during the running brand's surge, before taking the top job at Deckers.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his Nike career he ran the company's Italian and German subsidiaries before taking over footwear and then retail for all of Europe, Middle East and Africa; he earned his undergraduate degree at Middlebury College in Vermont.
notes: Consumer/footwear CEO, so weak fit for energy/data-center themes; possible entrepreneurship angle via HOKA's scaling story. Name appears in SEC data as 'Caroti Stefano'.

name: Mattias Stetz
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Rush Street Interactive (NYSE: RSI)
profile: Swedish-born Mattias Stetz (46) has been COO of online casino and sportsbook operator Rush Street Interactive (BetRivers) since April 2016, overseeing operations and its Latin American business. He spent 2004-2016 at Kindred Group (Unibet), serving as Chief Commercial Officer from 2009, and joined RSI as it built out US online gaming after state legalisation.
interesting_fact: He oversees RSI's Latin American business, one of the earliest US-listed online gaming operators to build a major presence in Colombia and Mexico.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MSc in Marketing and Business Development from the Stockholm School of Economics and is a Harvard Business School alumnus (General Management Program, 2015)—completed the year before he left Kindred for RSI.
notes: Low media profile; gaming sector, weak fit for energy/data-center. IR email confirmed via SEC full-text search of RSI 8-K press releases.

name: R. Scott Blackley
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Oscar Health (NYSE: OSCR); Director and Audit Committee chair, SLM Corp (Sallie Mae)
profile: Scott Blackley is CFO of health insurer Oscar Health (since 2021, with a 2022-23 stint as Chief Transformation Officer), overseeing treasury, actuarial, capital management and IR. Previously he was CFO of Capital One (2016-2021) and its Controller/Principal Accounting Officer (2011-2016), after roles at Fannie Mae, the SEC and KPMG.
interesting_fact: He moved from CFO of Capital One, one of the largest US banks, to CFO of then-recently IPO'd tech-driven insurer Oscar Health in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before corporate finance he worked at the US Securities and Exchange Commission (as well as Fannie Mae and KPMG); he holds a BS in Accounting from the University of Utah.
notes: Corporate finance executive, low personal media profile; health-insurance sector, weak fit for energy/data-center themes. Emails confirmed via SEC full-text search of Oscar press release filings.

name: Braden Michael Leonard
current_role: Founder and Managing Member, BML Capital Management LLC (Zionsville, Indiana)
profile: Braden (Brad) Leonard founded BML Capital Management in 2004 and runs BML Investment Partners, a concentrated, value-oriented fund that takes large stakes in small caps—recently mostly healthcare/biotech names such as Adverum, AN2 Therapeutics and Outset Medical (hence his SEC 10%-owner filings). Before BML he was an equity trader at proprietary trading firm ETG (1995-2003).
interesting_fact: As representative of Build-A-Bear Workshop's largest stockholder, he sat on the toy retailer's board from 2011 to 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career straight out of Purdue (accounting degree) as a proprietary equity trader at ETG, LLC from 1995 to 2003, then launched his own fund from Zionsville, Indiana rather than New York.
notes: Private Midwest investor with no website or published contact found; reachable only via BML Capital Management's SEC-registered office. Weak fit for energy themes; possible entrepreneurship/investing angle.

name: Scott E. Powell
current_role: Senior EVP and Chief Operating Officer, Wells Fargo & Company
profile: Scott Powell has been COO of Wells Fargo since December 2019, a key figure in the bank's regulatory remediation under CEO Charlie Scharf, with oversight of operations, control, regulatory relations and corporate properties. He was previously CEO of Santander Holdings USA and Santander Consumer USA, held senior consumer-banking and risk roles at JPMorgan Chase/Bank One, and began with 14 years in risk at Citigroup.
interesting_fact: He was recruited to Wells Fargo after leading a financial and regulatory turnaround at Santander Holdings USA, and as COO took on the bank's operations and regulatory relations during its post-scandal rebuild.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the board of trustees of Phipps Houses, one of New York City's oldest nonprofit affordable-housing developers; he holds a BA from the University of Minnesota and an MBA from the University of Maryland.
notes: Big-bank operator; route via Wells Fargo corporate communications/newsroom. Corporate properties remit gives a tenuous real-estate/energy angle; otherwise weak fit.

name: Thomas W. Florsheim Jr.
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Weyco Group (Nasdaq: WEYS); Director, Strattec Security Corp
profile: Thomas Florsheim Jr. has led Milwaukee-based footwear company Weyco Group (Florsheim, Nunn Bush, Stacy Adams, BOGS) as CEO since 1999 and chairman since 2002, succeeding his father, who ran the company for more than three decades. He has spent his entire ~40-year career at Weyco and has been a Strattec Security board member since 2012.
interesting_fact: His family name came full circle in 2002 when Weyco, under his leadership, acquired the Florsheim shoe brand; his father had been an executive at Florsheim Shoe Company before joining Weyco in the 1960s.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an executive he worked his way up inside Weyco in managerial roles, first running the retail division and then the purchasing department, becoming a VP in 1988.
notes: Family-company CEO; low media profile. No published IR/press email found on weycogroup.com. Brother John Florsheim is President/COO. Footwear sector, weak fit for energy themes; family-business entrepreneurship angle possible.

name: Morad Elhafed
profile: Morad Elhafed is a general partner at Battery Ventures, which he joined in 2008, focusing on growth and private-equity/buyout investments in software. He is one of the Battery fund managing members who share voting power over the firm's stakes—hence his SEC 10%-owner filings in Braze and Sprinklr; Battery filings also list him for Amplitude, ServiceTitan and Kodiak AI.
interesting_fact: As a Battery managing member he is named in the beneficial-ownership disclosures of several of the firm's big software IPOs, including Braze, Sprinklr, Amplitude and ServiceTitan.
notes: Low public profile; Battery's site (battery.com) was blocked to automated fetches, so bio details (joined 2008, software growth/buyout focus) come from third-party directories (theorg.com, mergr.com) and should be confirmed. Best route: Battery Ventures. Kodiak AI (autonomous trucking) holding is a possible tech angle.

name: Steven V. Abramson
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Universal Display Corporation (Nasdaq: OLED)
profile: Steven Abramson has helped build Universal Display (Ewing, NJ) since 1996—as President & COO until 2007 and CEO since 2008—into the pioneer of energy-efficient phosphorescent OLED (PHOLED) materials and IP, now used in more than a billion OLED smartphones. A lawyer by training, he earlier ran InterDigital's technology licensing division and was general counsel of Roy F. Weston.
interesting_fact: Universal Display's phosphorescent OLED tech—licensed from Princeton and University of Michigan research—is in over a billion smartphones; in 2026 he said the company is exploring adjacent organic electronics including organic solar cells.
deep_cut_fact: Before OLEDs he spent 1982-1991 at wireless pioneer InterDigital (then International Mobile Machines), rising from general counsel to EVP and GM of its Technology Licensing Division—the IP-licensing playbook he later applied to OLED.
notes: Good fit for energy-efficiency/deep-tech angle (OLED efficiency, blue PHOLED, organic photovoltaics). Regular conference presenter. Contacts from a 2023 press release (IR contact Darice Liu).

name: Frank C. Herringer
current_role: Independent Director (since 1996) and Nominating & Corporate Governance Committee chair, The Charles Schwab Corporation
profile: Frank Herringer, 83, is the former President (1986-99), CEO (1991-99) and Chairman (1996-2015) of Transamerica Corporation, which he sold to AEGON in 1999, later sitting on AEGON's Executive Board. He has been a Schwab director since 1996 and served on the boards of Amgen, Safeway and Cardax.
interesting_fact: Long before running Transamerica (of San Francisco's Transamerica Pyramid fame), he went on to lead its 1999 sale to Dutch insurer AEGON, and has since served three decades as one of Schwab's longest-tenured independent directors.
deep_cut_fact: In his early 30s he was President Nixon's Urban Mass Transportation Administrator (1973-75), a major architect of the National Mass Transportation Assistance Act of 1974, then left to become General Manager and CEO of San Francisco's BART system.
notes: Retired executive; no personal public channels found. Only route is via Charles Schwab corporate secretary/board contact process. Infrastructure/transit-policy background (UMTA, BART) could interest an energy/infrastructure podcast.

name: Philippe Botteri
current_role: Partner, Accel (London); Independent Director, UiPath (chairs nominating & governance committee)
profile: French-born venture capitalist Philippe Botteri has been a partner at Accel since 2011, investing in early and growth-stage cloud, security, AI and marketplace companies such as UiPath, Doctolib, Algolia and BlaBlaCar. Before Accel he spent about five years at Bessemer Venture Partners in Menlo Park, working on cloud investments like Cornerstone OnDemand and Eloqua. He sat on Fiverr's board (2016-2023).
interesting_fact: He has been on UiPath's board since 2020, after serving as a board observer from 2017, tracking the Romanian-founded automation company from startup to NYSE listing.
deep_cut_fact: He authors Accel's annual 'Euroscape'/'Globalscape' cloud-market reports; a recent edition framed AI as a race for compute, analysing hyperscaler spend on data-center infrastructure. He trained as an engineer at École Polytechnique and École des Mines.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/AI-compute theme via his Globalscape reports; frequent speaker at SaaStock and Paris Fintech Forum. No published personal email; route via Accel. Verify his social handles before use.
